papers.title: Mechanist: AI as a Scientific Instrument for Discovering the Mechanisms of Intelligence

summary.tldr: Mechanist is an agentic system that uses AI to autonomously discover, explain, and control the internal mechanisms of AI intelligence.
key_points: Integrates an interpretability knowledge graph of ~13,000 papers with a 43-million paper database across 26 fields.
Curates a library of 32 foundational methods for mechanism analysis, causal intervention, and validation.
Discovers cross-modality safety risk transfer from safe data and develops a mechanism theory of belief representation and emergence.
Executes practical interventions to improve model performance and steer scientific foundation models to generate targeted DNA sequences.
summary.why_it_matters: Automating mechanistic interpretability allows researchers to keep pace with rapid AI development, helping to identify safety risks and control model behaviors.

papers.title: DreamX-Phi 1.0: Action-Conditioned Video World Model for Robotic Manipulation

summary.tldr: DreamX-Phi 1.0 is an action-conditioned video world model for robotic manipulation that uses geometric attention encodings, depth prediction, and V-JEPA distillation to generate physics-faithful rollout observations.
key_points: Injects per-arm SE(3) transformations into attention via PRoPE-style geometric encoding to enforce arm identity and rigid-motion tracking.
Integrates a lightweight depth branch and uses SAM3 masks paired with a frozen V-JEPA teacher to enforce geometric and small-object consistency during manipulation.
Distills the multi-step generative model into a few-step student using distribution-matching distillation for faster real-time inference.
Achieved 1st place on Track 1 and 2nd place on Track 2 of the WorldArena 2.0 Challenge.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables fast and geometrically accurate simulation of robot actions, reducing the gap between visual realism and execution faithfulness in robotic world models.

papers.title: Intern-S2-Preview: Scientific Agentic Foundation Model

summary.tldr: Intern-S2-Preview is a scientific agentic foundation model series utilizing multimodal pre-training, agentic reinforcement learning, time-series forecasting, and an optional Memory Decoder module for long-horizon scientific tasks.
key_points: Uses a unified post-training pipeline incorporating supervised fine-tuning, multi-task RL, black- and white-box agentic RL, and on-policy distillation.

Features stability and efficiency techniques such as partial rollout with off-policy correction, adaptive length regularization, online speculative decoding, robust multi-task optimization, and trace-aware experience assembly.
Intern-S2-Preview-397B extends time series modeling to numerical forecasting and scientific signal understanding on SciTS.
Intern-MemDec-4B acts as a memory-augmented decoder that improves the Biology-Instructions score from 56.92 to 60.32 without altering the frozen 397B backbone.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables long-horizon, multimodal scientific reasoning and rapid domain specialization without needing to retrain large foundational model weights.

papers.title: AutoDesign: Meta-Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Design

summary.tldr: AutoDesign introduces a meta-harness optimizer that enables code agents to recursively improve model-harness systems through rollout feedback, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance on academic paper-to-poster generation.
key_points: Introduces PosterBench, featuring a 100-paper Main Track across five disciplines and a 10-paper PosterBench-mini subset for evaluation.
AutoDesign achieved a 78.32 score on PosterBench Main Track, outperforming Claude Design by 7.45 points.
Integrating the learned DesignHarness across seven controlled model configurations raised average PosterBench scores from 54.99 to 67.39 (+12.4%).
In a 40-minute long-horizon run under $3, the framework executed 253 tool calls and 11 editing turns to achieve average conference-poster quality.
summary.why_it_matters: The framework demonstrates that recursive meta-harness optimization significantly improves autonomous agent performance on complex multimodal media creation tasks at low cost.

papers.title: Alaya-EVOKE: From Linear-Scaling Supervision to Endless World

summary.tldr: Alaya-EVOKE is a three-step interactive world model that decouples long-horizon memory into an external world state bank and uses a linear-scaling teacher to achieve bounded-context, open-ended video generation.
key_points: Externalizes persistent scene geometry into a camera-indexed world state bank, retrieving only view-relevant data to keep the denoiser context bounded.

Redesigns the teacher model with sparse attention—combining chunk-wise grouping, distant frame retrieval, and a linear-attention global state—to achieve linear memory and compute scaling over long horizons.
Distills capabilities to a three-step, guidance-free student via a 30-second distribution-matching objective under self-forced rollouts to mitigate long-term content drift.
Generates a 1.5-second chunk (384x640 resolution) in 2.11 seconds on a single NVIDIA H200 GPU.
summary.why_it_matters: It resolves the trade-off between memory growth, low-latency interaction, and long-horizon consistency in real-time interactive video generation.

papers.title: Spatial Memory Agent: Experience-Grounded Procedure Memory for Spatial Intelligence

summary.tldr: The Spatial Memory Agent (SMA) is a parameter-update-free framework that enables frozen Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to improve spatial reasoning by distilling verified experiences into transferable lessons without using external spatial tools at inference.
key_points: SMA utilizes verifier-guided reflection on predicted answers and rewards to condense spatial experiences into compact, reusable lessons.
Lessons are assigned a Transfer Reliability Score (TRS), initialized uniformly and calibrated over time based on retrieval outcomes and transfer success.
Deployment uses a hybrid retrieval mechanism combining semantic filtering with a joint similarity-TRS ranking to guide the frozen VLM.
SMA achieved the highest macro average across four base VLMs and five spatial benchmarks, outperforming baseline methods in most of 20 evaluation settings.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a practical, tool-free method for VLM agents to self-evolve and improve spatial reasoning performance purely through experience without requiring model re-training or fine-tuning.

papers.title: PlayWorld: Benchmarking World Models with Agent Players over Long-Horizon Objectives

summary.tldr: PlayWorld is a new benchmark featuring 171 scenarios that uses multimodal Agent Players to evaluate interactive video world models on long-horizon objectives across core consistency and interaction dimensions.
key_points: Employs multimodal Agent Players to generate adaptive action sequences for evaluating world models against specific long-horizon goals.
Introduces PlayWorld, a benchmark comprising 171 target-driven evaluation scenarios.
Evaluates world models across four core dimensions: geometry consistency, interaction fidelity, out-of-sight evolution, and insight evolution, alongside video quality and controllability.
Benchmarking nine state-of-the-art world models shows widespread unreliability in spatial consistency and persistent state evolution during long-horizon interactions.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables standardized, objective-driven comparison of interactive video world models where fixed-action sequences fail due to variations in model dynamics.

papers.title: Massive Activations in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models: Pre-Attention Spikes and Inter-Spike Plateaus

summary.tldr: A systematic study reveals that hybrid linear attention LLMs exhibit two distinct massive activation morphologies: pre-attention spikes occurring right before full attention layers and inter-spike plateaus persisting across linear attention layers.
key_points: Identifies Pre-Attention Spikes (PAS) occurring immediately before full attention layers and Inter-Spike Plateaus (ISP) extending through intervening linear attention layers.
Validated patterns across 5 linear attention architectures, 6 hybridization configurations, 5 data domains, and open-source models ranging from 1.2B to 397B parameters.
Controlled pretraining of GDN-based hybrids up to 1.3B parameters demonstrates early emergence and asymmetric response to output gating.
Mechanistic analysis attributes PAS to a localized write-sink-cancel process, while ISP persistence results from delayed activation cancellation.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding these architectural activation patterns provides mechanistic insight into feature representation and stability dynamics across hybrid linear attention model designs.

papers.title: Self-Evolving Embodied Agents via Skill-Harness Evolution

summary.tldr: SHAPER is a self-evolving framework that adapts embodied agents to target environments without parameter updates by using a frozen foundation model to iteratively refine external reusable skills and a context-code harness.
key_points: Operates entirely train-free, maintaining frozen model parameters to eliminate the need for additional training runs, supervised fine-tuning data, or explicit reward signals.
Uses the same frozen foundation model to act as both the environment planner and the optimization agent that refines the system.
Evolves both non-parametric reusable skills and a context-code execution harness based on rollouts in target environments.
Evaluated on VLABench and ESI-Bench across agents with varying low-level action interfaces.
Outperforms baselines including pure execution, supervised fine-tuning, and test-time scaling methods like voting and verifier-free selection.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a practical method to continuously adapt embodied agents across diverse hardware interfaces without the compute cost or risk of fine-tuning model weights.

papers.title: Learning How the World Evolves: Extrapolative Video World Models via Latent Dynamics Reasoning

summary.tldr: Latent Dynamics Reasoning (LDR) casts video generation as explicit kinematic integration over structured latents, regressing only high-order residuals to enable physics extrapolation.
key_points: LDR executes numerical kinematic integration on structured latents, predicting third- and higher-order residual dynamics driving the video rollout.
Evaluated on the PhyWorld physics benchmark across five tasks (uniform motion, parabola, collision, bouncing, looming) at 256^2 resolution.
Reduces the gap between in-distribution and out-of-distribution error by over 20x compared to video diffusion baselines.
Requires 26x fewer parameters and operates 143x faster than the video diffusion baseline.
Generalizes across domain shifts, such as predicting the trajectory of a blue square moving right-to-left when trained only on red balls moving left-to-right.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates the first video world model capable of extrapolating physical laws out-of-distribution with significantly lower computational overhead than standard diffusion models.

papers.title: UniSwap: Streaming Audio-Visual Identity Swapping for Talking Videos

summary.tldr: UniSwap is the first streaming framework for joint audio-visual identity replacement in talking videos using a single audio-visual diffusion transformer.
key_points: Uses a swap-and-reconstruct training pipeline that strips visual and vocal identities from real clips to generate aligned cross-identity training targets.
Adapts a bidirectional backbone via In-context Pretraining, Conditional Streaming Adaptation (block-causal KV-cached generation), and Efficient Self-forcing DMD.
Reduces sampling iterations from 30 to 3 denoising steps per block while using Efficient Multi-LoRA Switching to share a single frozen backbone.
Employs Feature-RoPE Decomposition to keep cached positional embeddings within the training distribution for stable long-form generation.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables real-time, long-form talking video face-and-voice swapping within a unified architecture, eliminating the synchronization and consistency issues of decoupled audio and visual pipelines.

papers.title: LiveAnimate: Stable Long-Form Streaming Human Animation in Real-Time

summary.tldr: LiveAnimate is a 14B-parameter video DiT model enabling real-time, stable long-form streaming human animation at 19.63 FPS on two NVIDIA H100 GPUs.
key_points: Uses a two-stage pipeline consisting of Reference-Anchored Teacher-Forcing Adaptation to convert a bidirectional DiT into a block-causal generator, followed by Block-wise Self-Forcing Distillation to cut sampling to 3 steps.
Introduces Pose-Retrieval Sink Attention (PR-Sink), a bounded KV-cache using a Static Sink for the first block, a Dynamic Sink for pose-retrieved history, and a 3-slot Rolling Window.
PR-Sink maintains constant memory and per-block latency over extended durations without storing the full video sequence.
Employs Ulysses sequence parallelism and operator fusion to achieve 19.63 FPS real-time streaming inference.
Maintains constant perceptual quality and identity over a 3-minute benchmark, outperforming existing systems that suffer quality degradation or demand offline compute.
summary.why_it_matters: It resolves the trade-off between real-time latency and long-duration appearance stability, enabling responsive, interactive human animation for live streaming, telepresence, and virtual avatars.

papers.title: H2R-Bench: Benchmarking Human-to-Robot Manipulation Video Generation in World Models

summary.tldr: H2R-Bench is a new benchmark for evaluating how effectively video world models transform egocentric human manipulation videos into robot-centric manipulation videos across different embodiments.
key_points: Benchmark instances include an egocentric human demonstration video, target embodiment constraints, and annotations for task goals, action events, functional contacts, and object responses.
Evaluates generated videos across five key dimensions: goal-state completion, action-event completion, functional contact transfer, embodiment correctness, and overall video quality.
Benchmarked eleven state-of-the-art video generation models across six manipulation families and two distinct robot embodiments.
Results show current video world models struggle with embodiment consistency, functional interactions, and task execution.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a systematic diagnostic framework to determine if video world models can reliably convert abundant human video data into viable robot manipulation training resources.

papers.title: Persistent Recursive Worlds Enable Autonomous Software Evolution

summary.tldr: EvoX Genesis shifts software agent continuity from persistent agents to a persistent recursive world, enabling finite-lived agents to construct and redevelop large-scale codebases over long horizons.
key_points: Organizes software development through finite-lived agents proposing local changes, recursive delegation across paths, and persistent version history updates on accepted proposals.
Built a 250k-line Rust-based C compiler from scratch using DeepSeek V4 Flash over a 120+ hour run spanning >1,000 agent episodes for $44 in token costs.
Evaluated the generated compiler using the c-testsuite, LLVM tests, and Csmith, while demonstrating development continuation across agent replacements with GLM 5.2.
Reimplemented 13 Fortran MESA modules (100k+ lines) into a Rust workspace (90k lines), achieving median speedups of 1.55-6.87x across six numerical workloads.
summary.why_it_matters: Decoupling project continuity from agent lifespan allows low-cost, long-horizon software engineering and codebase modernization through interchangeable, finite-lived AI agents.

papers.title: Gaze Target Estimation Anywhere with Concepts

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced Promptable Gaze Target Estimation (PGE), creating the Gaze-Co dataset and GazeAnywhere, an end-to-end model that predicts gaze targets using natural language or visual prompts instead of multi-stage pipelines.
key_points: Promptable Gaze Target Estimation (PGE) unifies subject localization and gaze prediction, accepting text (e.g., 'the boy in the red shirt') or spatial coordinates as prompts.
The authors created Gaze-Co, a benchmark dataset containing 120,000 prompt-annotated image pairs using a custom scalable data engine.
GazeAnywhere utilizes a transformer detector fusing features from frozen encoders to jointly estimate subject localization, in/out-of-frame presence, and gaze target heatmaps.
GazeAnywhere established state-of-the-art results on PGE benchmarks and demonstrated robust generalization on an out-of-domain clinical dataset.
summary.why_it_matters: Replacing multi-stage pipelines with promptable, end-to-end gaze estimation prevents cascading detection errors and enables flexible, human-centric visual analysis across diverse real-world applications.

papers.title: Algebraic Decomposition Theory for Transformer Length Generalization

summary.tldr: Researchers established a complete algebraic characterization and polynomial-time decision algorithm to determine which regular languages transformers can length-generalize on.
key_points: Identifies that classical Krohn-Rhodes decomposition theory fails for C-RASP because building blocks like flip-flop and simple groups are inexpressible, while C-RASP's unbounded counting cannot be captured by finite semigroups.
Generalizes classical decomposition theory from finite semigroups to the infinite additive group on the integers, characterizing C-RASP via iterated wreath products of the integers.
Provides a decision algorithm running in polynomial time relative to the size of the regular language's syntactic monoid.
Validates the algebraic framework empirically across a broad test suite of regular languages to accurately predict transformer length-generalization behavior.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables a provable, algorithmic way to determine whether a transformer model can scale to longer sequences on specific formal language tasks without requiring empirical trial and error.

papers.title: Reduced Matrix Multiplication: Input-Adaptive Matrix-Product Reduction for LLM Inference

summary.tldr: Reduced Matrix Multiplication (RMM) is a training-free, input-adaptive inference method that speeds up Transformer models by selecting informative slices along contraction dimensions without altering weights.
key_points: Operates by selecting informative slices along matrix contraction dimensions controlled via a retention-ratio parameter.
Validated across 1B to 70B parameter models, discriminative and autoregressive tasks, long-context settings, and multimodal vision-language models.
Mechanistic ablations show structural asymmetry: attention-side computations tolerate far higher reduction than MLP components.
Demonstrated real-world speedups using custom kernels on an NVIDIA A100 GPU, particularly for longer sequence lengths.
summary.why_it_matters: RMM enables scalable, input-adaptive runtime acceleration and hardware-level FLOP reduction for large language models without requiring retraining or weight quantization.

papers.title: Rules or Character? Scaling Laws for AI Safety Design

summary.tldr: A novel comparative-statics model analyzes the optimal resource balance between character shaping and rule enforcement, showing that baseline character fragility under distributional shift drives safety design decisions far more than deployment scale.
key_points: Optimal safety resource allocation (alpha*) shifts weakly toward character shaping as deployment scale T increases, with shifts ranging from Delta alpha* = +0.01 to +0.21 across scenarios.

Baseline character fragility rate p^(0)_frag is the dominant parameter, altering alpha* by up to 0.50 across its range and exceeding the impacts of tail severity, filter quality, and common-mode failure probabilities.
Tail-risk (CVaR) and expected-harm optima converge at large deployment scales (T).
The safety model incorporates scale-dependent filter degradation, common-mode failures, character fragility, and a multiplicative Pareto damage distribution.
summary.why_it_matters: AI safety architects should prioritize improving the reliability of character shaping under novel conditions rather than relying primarily on deployment scale or inference-time output filtering.

papers.title: StateBridge: Training-free Hidden-state Alignment for Latent Communication in LLM Multi-Agent Systems

summary.tldr: StateBridge enables training-free latent communication between LLM agents by aligning final-layer hidden states to receiver input spaces using a closed-form orthogonal transformation with norm calibration and vocabulary anchoring.
key_points: Converts sender final-layer hidden states into a continuous prefix for the receiver, bypassing the discrete text bottleneck without using trained projectors.
Uses a closed-form orthogonal transformation paired with lightweight norm calibration and vocabulary anchoring to maintain compatibility with pretrained input distributions.

Outperformed the strongest baseline by achieving the best or tied-best score on 22 out of 26 model-task pairs across math reasoning, code generation, and question answering using four models from two families.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the information loss of text-based agent communication and the overhead of training cross-model projectors, offering a portable and lightweight hidden-state alignment method.

papers.title: Mixture of Training: Recombining Small-Scale Scaffolded Pretraining Runs into a Larger Language Model

summary.tldr: Mixture of Training (MoT) decomposes language model pretraining by training contiguous layer blocks inside frozen aligner scaffolds, then recomposing them into a single larger model that matches monolithic perplexity.
key_points: Partitions a target Transformer into contiguous layer blocks trained independently within frozen, pretrained aligner scaffolds.
Recomposes the trained depth slices into a single model, followed by an optional short end-to-end adaptation pass.
Evaluated on a 1.3B-parameter Gemma-style model using the C4 dataset.

Achieves perplexity parity with monolithic baselines, yielding a shorter layer-equivalent critical path after aligner preparation, though effective compute savings require reusing the aligners across runs.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a small-scale framework to test whether language model training can be broken down into modular, independently trainable layer units that are reconfigured and reused.

papers.title: vToken: Token-Level Virtualization for Reclaimable KV Caches

summary.tldr: vToken introduces a lightweight token-level virtualization layer that decouples logical token liveness from physical block allocation, resolving intra-block fragmentation caused by fine-grained KV eviction algorithms in LLM serving.
key_points: Uses a token-table indirection layer to maintain logical token views and repacks live tokens asynchronously into physical blocks without breaking PagedAttention kernels or CUDA Graph compatibility.
Integrated into vLLM with under 50 lines of code per policy, down from 500+ lines in conventional implementations.
Reduces retained KV blocks per request by 27.2% to 72.3% compared to a Naive-Evict baseline across eviction policies like H2O, Random, and Scissorhands.
Improves SLA-constrained throughput by up to 1.37x and doubles maximum feasible concurrency under constrained active-KV budgets.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables token-granularity KV cache eviction in block-based LLM serving frameworks like vLLM, maximizing memory efficiency and inference concurrency without custom hardware kernels.

papers.title: Teach the Magnitude, Not the Direction: Verifier-Bounded Credit Assignment for Multi-Turn Multi-step LLM Agents

summary.tldr: CrEST is a hierarchical credit assignment framework for multi-turn LLM agents that uses a privileged self-teacher to modulate update magnitudes while preserving reinforcement learning's verifier-bounded performance ceiling.
key_points: Resolves inter-turn reward dilution using turn-segmented verified advantages.
Mitigates intra-turn credit issues via entropy-gated self-teacher modulation of token-level update magnitudes.
Reduces the teacher's role from dictating update directions to regulating signal intensity, avoiding teacher-bounded ceilings and gradient concentration collapse.
Outperforms standard RL and distillation baselines on BFCL V3 and WildToolBench, showing peak gains on long trajectories and session-level metrics across two model scales.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables dense, token-level supervision for complex tool-use agents without suffering from policy collapse or capping performance below the verifier's ground-truth ceiling.

papers.title: DARTree: Speculative Diffusion Decoding with Autoregressive Draft Trees

summary.tldr: DARTree is a training-free speculative decoding method that extends an autoregressive correction head from draft chains to candidate trees, achieving up to 9.73x lossless speedup over autoregressive decoding.
key_points: Extends a pretrained autoregressive (AR) correction head to diffusion-generated draft trees to resolve unconditioned position-wise marginal distributions.
Decouples AR-head inference from sequential heap operations by batch-expanding and scoring all nodes at each depth to create a fixed-width tree before applying best-first pruning.
Accepts up to 12.97 tokens per verification round, representing a 98.6% increase over DFlash and a 27.9% increase over Domino under identical settings.
Outperforms prior methods in average acceptance length and speedup across seven math, code, and chat benchmarks in four model-temperature configurations.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly improves speculative decoding throughput and acceptance lengths without requiring additional model training or architecture modifications.

papers.title: When Local Variance Optimality Is Not Enough: RoPE-Aligned Q/K Rotations for Dynamic 4-Bit Quantisation

summary.tldr: Researchers proved only per-pair rotations commute with distinct-frequency RoPE, but found RoPE-aligned pairwise rotations increase perplexity compared to full-head Hadamard transforms in dynamic W4A4KV4 quantisation due to limited mixing support.
key_points: Proved the converse result that for distinct frequencies, no single-head orthogonal map commutes with RoPE other than per-pair two-dimensional rotations.
Derived the analytic rotation angle that minimises maximum channel variance under a position-averaged, pooled-covariance surrogate.
Found that replacing full-head Hadamard mixing with head-shared pairwise rotations degraded perplexity across four checkpoints in dynamic W4A4KV4 settings.
Demonstrated via controlled interpolation that increasing mixing support from 2 channels to full-head reduces key (K) range, relative quantisation error, and perplexity degradation.
Identified a structural mismatch: the local variance surrogate does not align with the tokenwise group-range statistic used by dynamic quantisers.
summary.why_it_matters: Optimal local variance reduction on structured mathematical surrogates is insufficient for post-training quantisation if the transform's channel mixing support fails to reduce tokenwise group ranges.

papers.title: Where You Measure Decides What You Measure: Position Selection in Ablation-Based SAE Evaluation

summary.tldr: Researchers show that standard ablation-based SAE evaluation measures effects at tokens dictated by the dictionary itself, introducing high variance that disappears when evaluations use a standardized, fixed token position.
key_points: Standard SAE evaluation measures ablation effects where a latent fires hardest, causing different dictionaries to be evaluated at different token positions.
Matching Google SAE latents by decoder similarity revealed that identical latent pairs frequently select different token positions for evaluation.
Evaluating six SAEs trained from a single initialization showed that inter-dictionary variance dropped from 7.6%-11.9% to near zero when measuring at the same token.
Increasing corpus size sixteenfold worsens position disagreement between dictionaries rather than mitigating it.
The authors propose a standardized evaluation protocol requiring reported causal numbers to explicitly fix and specify token positions.
summary.why_it_matters: Without controlling for measurement position, casual evaluation metrics reflect token selection noise rather than true structural differences between sparse autoencoders.

security.title: Concept Drift Detection and Adaptive Retraining of Malware Classification Models

summary.tldr: A novel One-Class Support Vector Machine (OCSVM) approach effectively detects concept drift in malware classification models, matching periodic retraining accuracy while significantly reducing computational overhead.
key_points: Evaluated OCSVM-based concept drift detection against Minibatch K-Means (MK-Means) and Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) statistical methods.
Tested performance across four baseline classifiers: Multilayer Perceptron, Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost).
Compared static, periodic, and drift-aware retraining scenarios using Pareto Front analysis to measure the tradeoff between accuracy and training efficiency.
Drift-aware retraining with OCSVM matched the classification accuracy of continuous periodic retraining while reducing the total number of retrained models, generally outperforming MK-Means and MMD.
summary.why_it_matters: Drift-aware retraining via OCSVM allows cybersecurity systems to maintain high malware detection accuracy against evolving threats without incurring the heavy compute costs of constant periodic retraining.

security.title: LLM-Assisted Dynamic Threat Analysis for Attacker-Reachable Software Weaknesses in Autonomous Vehicles

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated LLMs for generating dynamic exploitability test harnesses in the Autoware autonomous driving stack, finding that build integration and dependency wiring failures constitute the primary bottleneck rather than logic generation.
key_points: Compiler-precise static analysis of 185 Autoware packages identified 1,375 decision rules, 2,274 validation checks, and 482 input-to-safety-output flows.
Evaluating LLM generation across 740 sampled reachable sites yielded 3,700 artifact sets, where 80% of initial compilation failures stemmed from dependency wiring rather than program logic.
The tested reasoning model achieved a 64% first-shot compilation rate compared to 6% for the code-specialized model.
Full object-compileability required extensive stubbing, resulting in under half of the harnesses reaching the fuzzer and 37 observed crashes originating entirely in stubbed code rather than Autoware.
Zero candidate weaknesses were dynamically confirmed within the evaluation budget.
summary.why_it_matters: Automating software safety and security verification for autonomous vehicles using LLMs requires solving dynamic build integration and dependency resolution before LLM-generated fuzzing harnesses can successfully confirm vulnerabilities.

security.title: Does Fixing Break Security? An Empirical Study of Security Degradation in Iterative LLM-Driven Infrastructure-as-Code Repair

summary.tldr: An empirical study of 5,968 IaC-Eval timelines reveals that iterative LLM repair causes true security regressions in 3.3% of scenarios, primarily driven by resource restructuring and high code churn.
key_points: Analyzing 4,440 iteration transitions showed a standard regression rate of 13.8% of scenarios, but strict detection isolates true regressions to 3.3% of scenarios (5.2% of transitions) by filtering out multi-resource artifacts.
Resource restructuring accounts for 79.0% of root cause security regressions during LLM repair attempts.
Regression transitions exhibit 2.6x higher code churn (Cohen's d=0.90) and 4.9x higher strict-mode check volatility (d=1.49).
36.6% of standard-mode regressions self-correct within an average of 1.2 iterations, making iteration 3 the optimal stopping point.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that non-monotonic security degradation occurs during iterative LLM code repair, highlighting the need for security-aware feedback loops and optimal iteration budgets.

security.title: InterSAGE: The Secure and Verifiable Interoperability Protocol for An Internet of Agents

summary.tldr: InterSAGE is a four-layer, trust-native security protocol suite that provides persistent identity, capability-aware discovery, trust negotiation, and accountability for cross-organizational LLM agent interactions.
key_points: Agent Identity Cards bind developer, code package, operator, and deployment context to establish persistent agent identity.
Discovery uses DID-bound Verifiable Credential manifests for capability-aware peer searching.
Trust negotiation combines monotonic capability attenuation with a two-tier access control model.
Kernel-mediated cryptographic audit trails record usage, delegation, and execution traces without using a consensus ledger.
Designed to run alongside existing communication protocols like MCP, A2A, ANP, and AG-UI without replacing them.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a missing, standardized security layer that allows cross-organizational AI agents to verify identity, delegate authority, and maintain accountability without relying on centralized control or blockchain ledgers.

security.title: RAGSieve: Self-Referenced Local Contrast for Knowledge-Poison Detection in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary.tldr: RAGSieve is a self-referenced framework that detects knowledge-poisoning in RAG systems via query-local and corpus-local contrast without requiring poison labels, external reference corpora, or global thresholds.
key_points: RAGSieve-Query (RSQ) measures query-local contrast by scoring top-5 retrieved candidates against ranks 6-20 to identify answer-anchor concentration and carrier transitions at inference.
RAGSieve-Graph (RSG) evaluates corpus-local contrast during ingestion, comparing semantically similar but lexically distinct neighbors against local baselines to spot coordinated document density.
Evaluated across three QA datasets and six attack types, RSQ achieved 95.2% AUROC and RSG achieved 93.3% AUROC, outperforming existing baselines like GMTP and CleanBase.
Joint deployment of RSQ and RSG reduced attack success rates from 67.4% to 14.0% while preserving a 41.3% F1 score on clean retrievals.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables practical, two-tier defense against retrieval poisoning attacks at both corpus ingestion and query execution without depending on clean reference datasets.

security.title: ATOBench: Tracing How Autonomous Penetration-Testing Agents Verify Vulnerabilities When Target Evidence Lies

summary.tldr: ATOBench is an evaluation framework that probes how autonomous penetration-testing agents handle deceptive target evidence by comparing paired runtime-transformed and native attack trajectories across four process stages.
key_points: Injects registered runtime response transformations and pairs each transformed episode with an un-transformed native episode aligned at the first affected response.
Uses source-linked reconstruction to track downstream actions, evidence recovery, stopping decisions, and final report support.
Establishes three frozen observation contracts covering exploit proof, resource ownership, and reusable artifacts.
Evaluates five model routes across 450 episodes, revealing that higher agent activity can mask broken verification chains and that recovery relies on finding and preserving valid evidence.
summary.why_it_matters: It moves autonomous penetration-testing evaluation beyond binary end-goal success metrics by exposing how agents process, recover from, and report on deceptive or untrusted target observations.

security.title: Beyond Handcrafted Security: Towards Self-Evolving Defense for LLM Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers developed HARD, a framework that automates LLM agent runtime defense by iteratively evolving protection mechanisms based on observed failure traces.
key_points: Formulates runtime defense at the harness level to systematically integrate security mechanisms into the agent execution loop.
Introduces HARD (Harness-based Autonomous Runtime Defense Evolution), replacing manual engineering with an autonomous evolution process.
Automatically selects intervention strategies and iteratively optimizes defense artifacts using failure trace analysis.
Outperforms handcrafted runtime defenses in security evaluations while maintaining utility on benign tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables deployed LLM agents to continuously discover security vulnerabilities and autonomously upgrade their own runtime protections without requiring manual human intervention.

security.title: Labels Are Not Endpoints: Treatment Leakage and Construct Validity in MCP Agent Security Evaluation

summary.tldr: An audit of an MCP agent security evaluation revealed direct treatment leakage in the historical grader, where treatment metadata artificially gated attack labels without corresponding behavioral changes.
key_points: Audited 10,200 execution rows down to 180 model-bound requests and 15 observable stimuli, discovering that the planned payload-family corpus was never delivered.
A treatment-blind reconstruction reclassified 58 historical ATTACK_SUCCESS or HIJACK_ATTEMPT labels as authorized benign completions.
The corrected locked v2 census contained zero ATTACK_SUCCESS records, preserving only three verified protected-data transfers and one unauthorized-forwarding case.
A dual-reviewer blinded concordance review matched reviewer-consensus classes across 96 interpretable requests, but diverged from the locked codebook on four construct-boundary cases.
Introduced a seven-link Integrity Chain and an executable, scope-bounded endpoint-integrity linter to validate agent evaluation integrity.
summary.why_it_matters: Equating stored evaluation labels with actual agent behavior can lead to false security assessments if treatment metadata leaks into grading logic.

security.title: PIPES: Securing Agent Perception with Provenance and Priors

summary.tldr: PIPES mitigates agent state-corruption attacks by screening tool response units using static field contracts, source provenance metadata, and pre-response trajectories to enforce semantic priors.
key_points: Addresses state-corruption attacks where attacker-controlled content exceeds its informational authority to alter an agent's perceived environment.
Combines static field contracts for schema-based expectations with trajectory- and provenance-conditioned screening for open-ended content.
Enables flexible response actions upon detecting violations, including marking, warning, blocking, escalating, or atomic removal.
Reduces average attack success from 84.7% to 2.3% against Gemma 4 31B IT on VitaBench and AgentDyn benchmarks while increasing benign utility from 90.6% to 92.5%.
summary.why_it_matters: PIPES provides a structured defense that prevents untrusted external tool responses from manipulating an agent's environment state without sacrificing task performance.

security.title: Correct Is Not Governed: Provenance Integrity in Agentic Workflows

summary.tldr: Matrix is a deterministic causal-state layer that enforces governed execution in agentic workflows by tracking authority dependencies, verifying completion evidence, and selectively invalidating affected work.
key_points: Governed execution requires decisions, task completion, and updates to be backed by inspectable provenance rather than just correct outcomes.
Matrix records fact and authority dependencies to enable selective invalidation of downstream tasks when underlying facts change.
In controlled trials, direct and governed workflows yielded identical outcomes, but only governed workflows consistently retained audit evidence and blocked unsupported task closure.
A role-separated transfer test showed that strict completeness contracts can cause severe over-blocking on external, synthetic packets.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables institutional deployment of agentic AI by providing an independent integrity and auditing layer that ensures actions are verifiable, authoritative, and resilient to stale data.

security.title: Tracing Provenance and Detecting Tampering with Complementary LLM Watermarks

summary.tldr: A novel LLM watermarking method co-embeds robust and fragile signals into each token using independent keys and seeding windows, enabling concurrent provenance tracing and tamper detection.
key_points: Co-embeds a robust signal resilient to edits alongside a fragile signal sensitive to reader-visible changes within each generated token.
Employs unbiased tournament reweighting across multiple rounds to preserve the expected generation distribution.
Uses a periodic round-allocation pattern over normalized text to manage the trade-off between robust and fragile signal strength.
Maps detection scores to a two-dimensional decision space supporting three classifications: Intact, Tampered, and No-Watermark.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents piggyback spoofing by ensuring that adversarial edits to LLM-generated text trigger a tampered status rather than preserving valid attribution.

security.title: Privacy-Preserving RAG by Concealing Sensitive Information from External LLMs

summary.tldr: Researchers developed the Sensitive Entity Alias Generator (SEAG), a framework that obfuscates private entities in queries and retrieved documents using generated alias tables before sending them to third-party LLMs.
key_points: SEAG uses a lightweight model to identify sensitive entities, construct an entity replacement table, and swap sensitive words in queries and retrieved documents before external transmission.
Evaluating the framework on user accuracy (providing correct responses while hiding sensitive data) yielded over 80% accuracy across all tested models.
In evaluating complete entity hiding across documents, SEAG implemented with Qwen-3, LLaMA-3.2, and Phi-4 achieved total accuracies of 77.83%, 76.73%, and 74.91%, respectively.
Two new datasets were specifically constructed to fine-tune SEAG models and evaluate the end-to-end framework.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables organizations to leverage high-performing external LLM providers for Retrieval-Augmented Generation without exposing confidential query data or document contents to third parties.

security.title: Fingerprinting Text-to-Image Diffusion Models via Collapsed Generation

summary.tldr: A new non-invasive fingerprinting framework verifies text-to-image diffusion model ownership by identifying collapsed generation conditions where specific inputs yield highly consistent images across different stochastic seeds.
key_points: Exploits collapsed generation as an intrinsic, model-dependent behavioral signature without requiring invasive watermarking.
Supports white-box verification by injecting optimized continuous embeddings into the generation pipeline.
Supports black-box verification by querying natural language prompts through standard API service interfaces.
Demonstrates robust ownership verification across UNet- and transformer-based models under fine-tuning, query-level obfuscations, and low query budgets.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables model creators to detect intellectual property theft and unauthorized copying or fine-tuning of proprietary diffusion models without altering the model weights or degraded generation quality.

security.title: AI Guardrail Survival under Single-Cycle Agentic Self-Summarization

summary.tldr: Single-cycle agentic self-summarization often degrades safety rules into non-functional textual residues, causing significant behavioral violations even when constraints appear textually intact.
key_points: Textual presence of a safety rule does not guarantee execution; degraded residues increased prohibited actions by 34 and 57 percentage points over intact rules across two replay models.
Rule-form items are retained in context summaries substantially more often than prominence-matched facts, creating false assurance during audits.
Textual loss regimes depend on context budgets, exhibiting weld-or-drop with single rules and degraded predicate-loss under tighter budgets, while pure textual severing was not observed.
Silent runtime degradation requires external ground truth (like a constraint registry) to detect loss, though registries fail to detect if a surviving rule still fires.
Evaluation reliance on LLM-judge labels alone produced inaccurate conclusions that would have reversed experimental findings.
summary.why_it_matters: Auditing agent memory summaries for the mere presence of safety rules creates false assurance, as context compaction silently neutralizes guardrails without removing their text.

security.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Emerges as an Attack Enabler and Target in Cloud Security Alliance’s 2026 Top Threats Report

summary.tldr: The Cloud Security Alliance's 2026 Top Threats report highlights artificial intelligence as both a key attack enabler and a target, shifting security concerns away from traditional infrastructure.
key_points: Artificial intelligence has emerged as both a vector for enabling attacks and an direct target in cloud environments.
Identity, software supply chains, and interconnected cloud ecosystems have displaced traditional infrastructure as primary security concerns.
Findings are based on security practitioner feedback from the CSA's Top Threats to Cloud Computing Survey Report 2026.
summary.why_it_matters: Cloud security strategies must pivot from legacy infrastructure defenses to securing identities, AI pipelines, and supply chain interconnections.

infra.title: FP8 Training on AMD GPUs with TorchTitan and TorchAO: Upstreaming Performance Improvements

summary.tldr: AMD has upstreamed Primus-Turbo FP8 training optimizations into PyTorch's TorchAO and TorchTitan, enabling direct, high-performance FP8 execution on AMD Instinct GPUs.
key_points: Delivered a 13.4% training throughput gain over BF16 on dense Llama3-8B models using rowwise FP8 with weight-gradient GEMMs retained in BF16.
Integrated native hardware auto-detection for AMD's e4m3fnuz FP8 format (max value 240, no NaN/Inf) to resolve gradient corruption and clipping.
Built a Triton fusion pipeline for DeepSeek-V3 671B MoE shapes that recovered 89% of FP8 quantization overhead, including a 6.2x speedup per MoE layer via colwise scales coalescing.
Achieved a 4.2x backward pass acceleration on DeepSeek-MoE-16B by removing backward transposes and fusing kernels.
summary.why_it_matters: The upstreamed changes allow AI practitioners to leverage out-of-the-box, highly optimized FP8 training on large-scale AMD Instinct MI300X clusters without relying on external, out-of-tree libraries.
